# Selected-product AO fixture

All content is synthetic. `account/` selects alpha from a multi-nested alpha/beta account at toolkit `e9dce951ab4cd6aa9ccc734df96590bde25ccde9`, schemaVersion 8. Knowledge notes stay at the account root. Model rows come from the selected product and eligible account rows. The read-only documents of SPEC-0135 R2 sit at both roots: `_moc.md` and `_improvements/shared-idea/` at the account root, and `MOCs/alpha-map.md` and `_improvements/alpha-idea/` under `products/alpha/`, with one curation document, `.kb/curation/review-log.md`; the generated admission keeps the account root and alpha's root.

`intermediate.json` was captured through the starter's read-only adapter against that pinned AO library. Its `oracle.rows`, `edges`, and `unresolvedEdges` come from AO's own reader. `oracle.knowledge` records AO `product_notes` with the graph's `placed()` behavior for assertions/concepts (nonrecursive), and recursive sources/artifacts. It includes shared wildcard, selected, absent-products and alpha-folder assertions; beta, explicit empty-products and unselected colliding IDs are excluded.

AO `edges()` omits claim targets. A scratch-only Python helper derived `oracle.evidence` from each AO-resolved row's ordered `supported_by`/`rests_on` values with AO's evidence-edge rule (kb-site `trace.py`): an exact file stem of a selected assertion first, else an exact frontmatter `id`. One match means resolved, zero means unresolved, multiple means ambiguous; `.md`, path and case variants stay unresolved. This preserves repeated authored occurrences and refuses an arbitrary winner. The helper checked every resolved pair against AO's own trace graph and recorded `oracle.aoEvidenceEdges`: AO draws 11 unique evidence edges, 2 of them its arbitrary pick for a repeated ID (`a-ambiguous`) or stem (`selected`), so Rhizome must draw the other 9. The account and beta model IDs collide with alpha's while remaining outside alpha's selected projection. The alpha project override adds `feature.project_detail`. Each product's `product.yaml` lists `metamodel.yaml` under `owns`; without it, AO's product commands copy the account's metamodel over the product copy (`product.mirror_config`) and drop the override, and the adapter resolves the account file the same way.

The checked intermediate and literal SDL are CI inputs. CI never imports AO or runs Python. The Go provider parity suite in `testdata/ao-kb-model` projects this fixture alongside the booking journey through the real providers and compiled bindings. See that directory for commands.
